title: On	1call & Incident Response Playbook 	6	6 Comprehensive
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's on‑call and incident response practices: severity definitions, detection and triage flows, runbook templates, postmortem expectations, rotation rules, game day guidance, and status‑page / customer communications templates. It is intended for all engineering teams that operate production services and for on‑call responders across Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Scope

- Applies to all production incidents affecting customer availability, data integrity, or security.
- Excludes: non‑production test environments, local developer builds, and purely exploratory research experiments.

Roles & Responsibilities

- Primary on‑call (Responder): first line — triage, mitigation, and initial communications.
- Secondary on‑call (SWE): escalation target for unresolved incidents or when additional domain knowledge is required.
- Incident Commander (IC): takes ownership for major incidents (P0/P1) — coordinates cross‑team activity and external comms.
- SRE Lead / Pager Escalation: enforces SLOs, capacity decisions, and postmortem ownership.
- Communication Owner: publishes status updates and customer notifications.
- Postmortem Author: documents root cause, timeline, and corrective actions.

Incident Severity & SLOs

Severity classification is used for routing, escalation, and postmortem requirements. Use the following as a guide: 

1) P0 — Sev0 (Major outage)
- Impact: System wide outage or >50% of customers affected, or data loss.
- Target response: Primary on‑call acknowledges within 5 minutes. IC engaged within 15 minutes.
- Required actions: Immediate mitigation, continuous updates every 15 minutes on status page.
- Postmortem: Blameless postmortem required within 72 hours (draft) and published within 14 days.

2) P1 — Sev1 (Service degraded)
- Impact: Significant degradation to critical functionality (10–50% of customers) or severe latency regressions that violate latency SLOs.
- Target response: Acknowledge within 15 minutes. Escalate to Secondary within 30 minutes if unresolved.
- Updates: Status page every 30–60 minutes.
- Postmortem: Postmortem required within 7 days.

3) P2 — Sev2 (Partial impact)
- Impact: Localized customer impact, non‑critical features, or intermittent errors.
- Target response: Acknowledge within 1 hour.
- Updates: Internal updates as needed; external status page optional.
- Postmortem: Postmortem at discretion of owner if recurring or high cost.

4) P3 — Sev3 (Informational / maintenance)
- Impact: Planned maintenance, low‑impact bugs, or cosmetic issues.
- No on‑call escalation required beyond normal bug triage.

Incident Lifecycle (High level)

1. Detection & Alerting
- Sources: Prometheus / Grafana alerts, Sentry, internal healthchecks, automated chaos detectors, customer reports (support tickets).
- First responder acknowledges in the pager / Slack #incidents channel and begins triage.

2. Triage
- Quickly determine scope and severity. Key questions: Which customers/regions are affected? Is there data loss? Is there a security component?
- Use telemetry dashboards (latency, errors, CPU/GPU utilization, network, KV cache hit rates).

3. Mitigation & Containment
- Apply short‑term mitigations (traffic re‑routing, fallback to smaller model variant, scale up Dedicated capacity, disable failing feature flag).
- If mitigation may impact customers (e.g., degraded model quality), coordinate Messaging Owner before changes.

4. Recovery & Verification
- Restore service to compliant levels, run smoke tests, and verify both functional and performance characteristics.
- Confirm with monitoring and a representative sample of customer traffic.

5. Post‑incident & Postmortem
- Create a postmortem on the corresponding Confluence template. Include timeline, root cause analysis (RCA), impact summary, action items with owners and ETA, and regression test additions.

Runbook Templates & Examples

Each critical service must maintain a short runbook with: detection criteria, key dashboards, common mitigations, rollback steps, and owner contact information. Below is an abridged runbook template for the Text Generation API gateway: 

Runbook: Text Generation API Gateway (abridged)
- Owner: Platform Gateway Team (oncall: gateway‑oncall@pagerduty)
- Detection criteria: 5xx error rate > 0.5% for 5 minutes AND 95th percentile latency > 1200ms for 5 minutes.
- Key dashboards: /grafana/d/abc123/text‑gateway‑overview, /grafana/d/def456/kv‑cache‑metrics
- Initial mitigation steps (ordered):
  1. Verify alert: check Grafana and Sentry for correlated errors.
  2. Rollback last deployment: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/text‑gateway -n prod`
  3. If rollback ineffective, scale gateway pods: `kubectl scale deployment/text‑gateway --replicas=6 -n prod`
  4. Enable model fallback: update traffic routing to model‑variant v1.2‑safe via router CLI: `rictl router set‑route --service text‑gen --variant v1.2‑safe`
  5. If suspected KV cache corruption, flush read cache on affected pool: `redis-cli -h cache‑pool-2 FLUSHDB` (execute only with approval of SRE Lead).
- Escalation steps: contact Secondary on‑call, then SRE Lead.
- Post‑mitigation checks: Synthetic trace success, 95th pctl latency < 800ms sustained for 10 minutes.

Example runbook script (JSON snippet for runbook registry):
{
  "service": "text‑gateway",
  "owner": "platform‑gateway",
  "escalation_policy": "gateway‑policy",
  "check_command": "curl -sSf https://health.textgateway.prod/ready"
}

On‑call Rotations & Escalation Policy

- Rotation cadence: Primary on‑call rotates weekly for most engineering teams; SRE rotations are 7 days with 1 week of overlap on handoffs.
- Handover checklist (to be completed in team Slack #oncall‑handover and as a short Confluence note):
  - Current ongoing incidents and mitigations.
  - Upcoming releases or maintenance windows.
  - Pager fatigue or unresolved follow‑ups.
  - Contactable escalation points for the week.
- Escalation policy (example):
  1. Primary on‑call (ack within X min).
  2. After 15 minutes for P0 / 30 minutes for P1, escalate to Secondary.
  3. If unresolved after 60 minutes (P0) escalate to IC and SRE Lead.
  4. For security incidents, immediately loop in Security team and follow the security incident checklist.

Game Days (Practice & Readiness)

- Frequency: Each team must run at least two game days per quarter. SRE coordinates cross‑team scenarios twice per year.
- Goals: Validate runbooks, test fallback paths, verify oncall coverage, and exercise customer comms.
- Example scenarios: sudden GPU fleet outage, KV cache corruption, model regression causing hallucinations, cross‑region network partition.
- Post game day: publish AAR (After‑Action Report) with improvements and runbook updates.

Status Page & Customer Communication Templates

Use the company status page for all externally visible incidents affecting customers. Communication Owner is responsible for publishing updates. Below are templates: 

Initial public incident (T+0)
Title: Partial outage affecting Text Generation API — investigating
Body: We are currently investigating increased errors and latency for the Text Generation API affecting some customers in us‑west. Our on‑call team is actively investigating. We will provide an update in 15 minutes.
Impact: Some requests may return 5xx errors or experience increased latency.
Mitigation: We are rolling back a recent router change and running mitigations to restore capacity.\n
Regular update (example)
Time: 2026‑01‑02 14:15 UTC
Update: Investigation continues. We have rolled back the latest router change and scaled gateway pods to mitigate increased latency. Error rate has dropped from 2.3% to 0.7% over the last 15 minutes. We are monitoring. Next update in 30 minutes.

Resolution notice
Title: Incident resolved — Text Generation API restored
Body: The Text Generation API is restored to normal operation. The root cause appears to be a regression in the router traffic split logic introduced in deployment v2026.01. We have rolled back the change and validated recovery with synthetic traffic. A detailed postmortem will be published within 7 days.

Customer escalation template (for account teams)
Subject: Incident affecting Text Generation API — immediate action and customer impact
Body: Hello <CustomerName>,
We identified an incident on <date/time> that affected your requests to the Text Generation API. Impact: intermittent 5xx responses and higher latency between <start> and <end>. Mitigation: traffic was routed to a safe variant and capacity was increased to restore service. We will share a postmortem and compensatory credit guidance (if applicable) once the RCA is complete. For urgent concerns, please contact your PM or support@redwood.ai.

Postmortem Requirements & Template

Minimum postmortem fields for P0/P1:
- Title and incident timeline (UTC)
- Summary and impact (customers, revenue, internal ops)
- Root cause(s) and evidence
- Action items (owner, due date, verification steps)
- What went well / What went poorly
- Follow‑ups and regression tests added
- Sign‑offs: IC, SRE Lead, Product Manager

Timeline expectations: Draft within 72 hours (P0) or 7 days (P1); final published by 14 days (P0) or 21 days (P1).

Monitoring & Dashboards (recommended)

- Alert types: 5xx error rate, 95th/99th pctl latency, GPU OOMs, KV cache hit rate, queue length, model response correctness (sampling), downstream dependency failures.
- Dashboards: Service overview, per‑region trailing indicators, per‑model latency heatmaps, autoscaler health, and deployment change history.

Escalation Matrix & Contacts

- PagerDuty groups: platform‑gateway, serving‑runtime, model‑onboarding, s3‑storage, netops.
- Oncall contact book: stored in Confluence contact table and synced to PagerDuty. For immediate security escalation: security‑oncall@redwood.ai

Appendix: Playbook Maintenance & Training

- Review cadence: Teams must review and update runbooks quarterly, and after any incident where the runbook was used.
- Training: New on‑call engineers must shadow an experienced on‑call for two rotations and attend a game day within first 90 days.
- Ownership: Runbook owners are responsible for accuracy, and SRE will audit key runbooks monthly.

Quick reference — Commands & Links

- Rollback deployment: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/<service> -n prod`
- Scale: `kubectl scale deployment/<service> --replicas=<n> -n prod`
- Router CLI example: `rictl router set‑route --service <svc> --variant <variant>`
- Health endpoint check: `curl -sSf https://health.<service>.prod/ready`
- Grafana: /grafana/d/ (team dashboards)

Contact & Ownership Table (short)

- Platform Gateway — Owner: Diego Morales — pager: platform‑gateway
- Serving Runtime — Owner: Priya Singh — pager: serving‑runtime
- SRE Lead — Owner: Liam O'Connor — pager: srel‑lead

Document change log

- 2025‑11‑15: Created (Aisha Patel).

End of playbook. For questions or to request a runbook audit, contact the SRE program manager at sre‑program@redwood.ai.
